dominant_breach: fraud controls and identity proofing can protect public funds while also locking legitimate unemployed workers out of timely benefits unless due-process, non-digital, and restoration rails are built in
fastest_washout: identity-proofing failure, account takeover, claimant hijacking, legacy IT, documentation burden, and payment suspension wash out unemployment insurance as a shock absorber

remedy_operability_gate.note: UI access must balance fraud prevention with prompt claimant relief; identity proofing becomes a remedy gate when failure blocks income replacement.

identity_proofing_exclusion_risk.note: Fraud controls and identity proofing are legitimate, but active scoring requires offline, assisted, appeal, and payment-restoration rails when identity proofing blocks a legitimate claimant.

anti_fraud_due_process_balance.note: DOL, NIST, and GAO sources support fraud-risk controls; the certification issue is whether due process and restoration keep pace with payment suspension.

non_digital_access_channel.note: DOL identity-verification guidance and NIST digital-identity rules make non-digital and usability protections an operational proof burden.

administrative_burden_lockout.note: Claim hijacking, account takeover, authentication, documentation, and in-person proofing burdens can convert a right into a lockout problem.

benefit_payment_timeliness.note: Payment holds, identity-fraud remediation, and legacy UI systems can defeat UI as a shock absorber unless timeliness and restoration are measured claimant-by-claimant.

remedial_data_logging_and_auditability.note: Risk controls should log false positives, manual-review time, non-digital use, and claimant restoration, not only fraud interdiction.

gate_11_enforceability_remedies.why: A locked-out worker needs a fast manual path, interim protection, and restoration after erroneous suspension.

gate_17_score_mediated_exclusion.why: Identity systems can become score-mediated exclusion when false negatives or unresolved flags block payment.

gate_07_public_common_counterweight.why: UI is a public counterweight only if integrity controls do not make legitimate claimants residual to fraud prevention.

remedy_operability_register.harm_or_claim: Unemployed claimant blocked, suspended, or hijacked by identity verification/fraud-control process
remedy_operability_register.claimant_perimeter: Workers seeking UI benefits, including claimants without stable digital access, documentation, devices, credit files, or English fluency
remedy_operability_register.standing_path: State UI agency claim, identity challenge, manual review, appeal, and fraud/identity-theft reporting
remedy_operability_register.notice_explanation: Claimants need clear notice of the exact block, the evidence needed, vendor role, deadline, and manual alternative
remedy_operability_register.interim_protection: Uncertified; scoring should require time-limited provisional payment or hardship exception where risk is unresolved but claimant continuity is urgent
remedy_operability_register.time_to_relief: Must measure days from lockout or suspension to restored payment, not only final fraud adjudication
remedy_operability_register.review_body: State UI agency, vendor review channel, manual adjudicator, appeal tribunal, DOL oversight
remedy_operability_register.collective_or_representative_action: Ombud, claimant advocate, legal-aid, and pattern-reporting channels are needed because many lockouts are too small and urgent for individual litigation
remedy_operability_register.restoration_remedy: Restore benefits, correct tax/1099 and identity records, compensate fees/overdrafts where caused by wrongful block, and repair account access
remedy_operability_register.enforcement_actor: State UI agencies, DOL/ETA, DOL-OIG, vendors, state appeal tribunals, federal oversight

case_notes: rev0332 active finding: UI identity proofing is not just an anti-fraud integrity case; it is an access/remedy case where legitimate claimants must have fast assisted routes and restoration after false positives.
